definition: Interest that is added to the balance at the end of each period and then earns interest itself; at a nominal annual rate of $r\%$ compounded $k$ times a year, the balance is multiplied by $1 + \frac{r}{100k}$ each period.

The loss of an item's value over time; at a fixed rate of $r\%$ a year the value is multiplied by $1 - \frac{r}{100}$ each year, so in this model it falls by a smaller amount each year and never reaches $0$.

The value at the start ($PV$), such as the amount invested or borrowed; in a calculator's finance solver with no regular payments, it has the opposite sign to the future value, because the money moves the other way.
The value after a given number of periods ($FV$); in a calculator's finance solver with no regular payments, it has the opposite sign to the present value, because the money moves the other way.
What a future amount of money is worth in today's prices once inflation, the yearly percentage rise in prices, is allowed for; it is less than the future value whenever inflation is positive.
